timeline.current_model: FASN is the sole multifunctional enzyme catalyzing de novo long-chain fatty acid synthesis from acetyl-CoA, malonyl-CoA and NADPH; it is regulated at the transcriptional level by SREBP-1/Sp1/FBI-1 and at the protein level by multiple E3 ligases (FBXW7β, TRIM21) that drive K48-ubiquitination/proteasomal degradation, counteracted by deubiquitinases (USP13, USP2) and by palmitoylation at specific cysteine residues (catalyzed by ZDHHC20 at C1471/C1881 and ZDHHC21 at C1317, and opposed by ZDHHC21 in some contexts); the palmitate it produces also drives palmitoylation of downstream signaling proteins including MYD88 (at C113, enabling IRAK4 recruitment), MHC-I (targeting it for lysosomal degradation via DHHC3), PD-L1, and mutant p53 (stabilizing gain-of-function mutp53), thereby coupling lipid metabolism to innate immune signaling, antigen presentation, immune evasion, and oncogenesis; FASN activity is additionally required for radial glia cell polarity and brain development, surfactant phospholipid homeostasis in alveolar type II cells, and autophagosome-lysosome fusion via interaction with SNARE complexes.
